subject: PO 4521 — invoice windowing, PO mapping, and net terms options
messages:
From: AP Team <accounts-payable@medflow.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medflow.com>, Lisa Chang <lisa.chang@medflow.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PO 4521 — invoice cadence and PO split questions

Hi Olga,

Quick one from procurement as we're getting PO 4521 into our ERP: our AP policy requires either (a) separate invoices per cost-center (we have 4 cost centers for this engagement) or (b) a single invoice with each line tagged to the cost center and the external PO number present in the invoice header.

A few constraints from our side:
- Net terms we need on vendor records are Net45 (company policy),
- Invoices must arrive in weekly batches (Mon-Fri) to match our weekly remittance run,
- We need the PO number and a PO lock reference in the electronic invoice metadata so our system can auto-apply.

Also — is there any flexibility on pricing if we consolidate billing monthly instead of weekly? Our procurement lead asked whether a consolidated monthly invoice would qualify for a volume/commitment discount.

I've attached the PO we created (MedFlow_PO_4521.pdf) for reference.

Can you confirm Redwood's ability to:
1) Accept a single PO and map invoice lines to cost centers, or
2) Emit multiple invoices per PO on a weekly cadence, and
3) Apply an agreed discount if we switch to monthly consolidated billing?

Thanks,
Lisa Chang
MedFlow Health — Procurement
accounts-payable@medflow.com
(attachment: MedFlow_PO_4521.pdf)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chang <lisa.chang@medflow.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO 4521 — invoice cadence and PO split questions

Hi Lisa — thanks for the clear summary and the PO. Quick answers up front: yes, we can support either approach but there are tradeoffs, and we have two pragmatic options to propose.

Option A — Single PO, consolidated monthly invoice (default at Redwood):
- One invoice per month referencing PO 4521 in the invoice header,
- Each invoice line will include a cost-center code (we can map your 4 codes to line items),
- This is our lowest operational cost option; we can offer a 2.0% billing credit applied to monthly invoices when a 12-month commitment is on file.

Option B — Weekly invoice windowing (requested by your AP):
- We can emit weekly invoices tied to PO 4521 and include the PO lock metadata so your ERP auto-applies them,
- Operationally this adds invoice processing overhead on our side; to cover that we propose either a small processing fee (0.5% of invoice value) or rolling the fee into pricing with no credit.

On Net terms: our standard for enterprise accounts is Net30. We can accept Net45 for this customer with an alternate payment plan — specifically, Net45 with a 1.25% early-payment discount if payments are received within 15 days. That preserves your Net45 requirement but provides a modest incentive to accelerate cash.

To proceed we'll need:
- Confirmation of which option you prefer (A or B),
- The exact cost-center codes to map across invoice lines, and
- A remit address and vendor code (if your ERP requires specific vendor IDs).

I'm attaching a short SOW with the billing carve-outs highlighted (SOW-v2.docx). If you prefer, Marcus and I can jump on a 20-min call tomorrow to lock the MA plan for onboarding.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Sr. Sales Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
(attachment: SOW-v2.docx)

Thanks, Olga — that helps. A couple of clarifying items before we pick an option:

1) The 2.0% credit for monthly consolidation — is that a one-time credit applied to the first invoice (to offset switching costs), or an ongoing percentage discount on billings for the life of the contract?
2) If we go weekly, what is the operational lead time to set up weekly lanes and the PO lock metadata so our ERP picks them up automatically? We need this working before our first remittance window (week of Sep 20).
3) For Net45 + early-payment discount: how will that appear on the invoice and in your remittance matching? We prefer discounts to be shown as a separate line item (e.g., Early Payment Discount 1.25%) so our AP team can validate.

Also — Procurement asked whether Redwood can handle multiple PO numbers under the same deal (we sometimes issue a master PO + supplemental POs per quarter). Will Redwood accept supplementary POs tied to the same SOW?

If it helps, I can share an AP spec document that lists our invoice metadata fields (PO lock, remit ID, cost center tags).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Lisa
MedFlow Health

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO 4521 — invoice cadence and PO split questions

Lisa — great questions, and thank you. Here is a recommended compromise that aligns with both teams' constraints and keeps your AP automation intact:

Agreed approach (recommended):
- Start with weekly invoice windowing for the first 60 days to match your AP run and validate PO lock automation. Redwood will emit invoices every Friday and include PO 4521 in the invoice header and the PO lock metadata field.
- After the 60-day validation period, switch to consolidated monthly billing if both sides agree; at that point the 2.0% ongoing billing credit can be enacted from month 1 of consolidation. The credit is ongoing (applies to each consolidated monthly invoice while the 12-month commitment is active).
- Net terms: Redwood will record Net45 on the vendor record. We will show an explicit line on each invoice for "Early Payment Discount — 1.25% (if paid within 15 days)" so your AP can validate and apply the discount in their remittance system.
- Multiple POs: we can accept supplemental POs tied to the same SOW. Please place the master PO number in the header and list supplemental PO numbers as invoice references; we'll map them in our billing engine.

Operational items for your AP (action items):
1) Share the AP spec listing the metadata fields (PO lock key name and remit ID) — we'll map these into our invoice XML.
2) Confirm the exact cost-center codes for line mapping (four codes).
3) Confirm vendor code and remit address (electronic remit preferred).

Next steps: Marcus will create a short mutual action plan (MAP) in HubSpot and add the billing milestones. I'll attach a brief PDF that shows the invoice window naming convention and an example invoice (Invoice-Window-Spec.pdf). If you can confirm items 1–3 by EOD Mon 9/13 we'll schedule the first weekly invoice for Fri 9/17.

If you want to accept this approach, please reply with "Approve weekly onboarding" and we'll kick off the MAP.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Sr. Sales Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
